beats.caption: Normally the GPU's controller drives every DRAM command
beats.text: While the accelerator is busy, its memory controller sends a constant stream of ACTIVATE, READ, WRITE and REFRESH commands to the HBM stacks. Refresh is the controller's job: it must hit every row about every 64 ms.

beats.caption: Self-refresh entry: the controller goes quiet
beats.text: When memory will sit idle, the controller issues a self-refresh entry command and stops talking. The DRAM takes over its own refresh, so the link and the controller's PHY can power down.

beats.caption: The DRAM's own timer refreshes each row in turn
beats.text: An internal oscillator and row counter inside the die open and rewrite rows one after another, keeping every cell inside its retention window. The data stays valid with no outside commands.

beats.caption: Only refresh draws power; the interface sleeps
beats.text: Clocks, I/O drivers and receivers are off, so the device draws a few milliwatts instead of watts. Many parts also adjust the refresh rate to temperature, refreshing less often when cool.

beats.caption: Exit takes time, so it suits idle memory, not training
beats.text: Leaving self-refresh needs a wake-up delay of hundreds of nanoseconds before commands resume, so busy training jobs never use it. It matters for idle nodes, system suspend and memory power budgets. Related: Micron (MU), SK hynix (000660.KS), Rambus (RMBS).
